description: Issue #839 AC1: `define foo` twice is an ERROR, not a silent override. Phase-1 registration raises `ol-duplicate-definition` carrying BOTH spans — `source_span` at the later declaration, `params.original_span` at the earlier one (`spec/error-model.md:126,144-147`) — and `spec/execution-model.md:86-88` makes it "MUST NOT be a silent override". The two bodies print DIFFERENT values on purpose, so the fixture discriminates between all three candidate rules — last-wins prints `222`, first-wins prints `111`, and only the ruling's rule produces the empty event stream asserted here. The `foo` call on line 7 is likewise deliberate: it proves nothing runs at all, rather than merely that the definitions were rejected. Core Language only, because phase-1 registration is unconditional — no profile decides whether a program may declare a name. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
